answer.answer: Audit-ready reconciliation completed and persisted as checkpoint `checkpoint:7e8289b5-0d39-2827-94c2-4c4306780cbf`. The verified archive remains preserved as historical evidence; the existing canonical snapshot remains unchanged; selectively promoted evidence is distinguished from deduplicated corpus data; and rejected Flowworks work is fenced off from current guidance.

claims.value: The original `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` is preserved losslessly with its verified extracted tree under the Git-ignored `raw/` directory. The ZIP is exactly 21,674,717 bytes with SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`; it contains 123 entries including directories, with 115 manifested files plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`. `unzip -t` passed and every packaged SHA-256 passed. `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` remain tracked so the ignored duplicate third-party corpus, personalized save context, generated binaries, and legacy SQLite database remain auditable without placing them in Git.

The archive’s numeric data must not be labeled build `23761620`: that was only the latest public executable observed, Hotfix `0.2.8`. The authoritative two-axis boundary is (1) the source/game-data claim: Update 1, internal game version `35118973`, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441`—inferred `0.2.0`; and (2) the source snapshot: SRDB `2.3.4`, updated 2026-07-10 and retrieved `2026-07-11 05:02:30 UTC`. The immutable canonical snapshot is `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`. Archive reports retain their `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z` legacy capture boundary and cannot receive the canonical snapshot ID unless ported and rerun against it.

The archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were semantically deduplicated against the richer RuptureOps corpus and were not installed as a competing game-data snapshot. Selective promotion was limited to the player save baseline `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`; six medium-confidence Ore Excavator v2 impure/pure recipe-producer associations; explicit consumable-effect assumptions kept separate from raw item records with provenance warnings; nine player-specific site/geography assets; and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected two normalization defects: `airlock` had been overwritten by a building-shaped detail response, and Training Corporation retained a literal `$undefined` index. No second canonical game-data snapshot was created.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is preserved only as superseded audit history; its buffer-heavy model, five-output-depot bank, second permanent HRS export depot, prebuilt separate Helium rail, and overbuilt three-Stabilizer/two-slow-press direction must not become current guidance. The July 11 progression note is authoritative and describes a plan, not confirmed construction: the starter has one Stabilizer, one Impeller, and one Turbine; the Valve expansion adds one Nozzle and two Valves; the Pressure Tank stage adds two Pumps; the second Stabilizer comes later before Scanner/levels 11–12; and HRS v2 is reserved as an evidence-triggered recovery option, built only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. The active RuptureOps pipeline/database and this staged plan supersede the archive’s SQLite database, snapshot JSON, delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh/query scripts, and rejected calculations.

answer.answer: The three dumps are reconciled as lossless provenance, not three competing saves. Repeated material remains exact history but produces one canonical fact; only unique, properly classified player evidence is promoted. The durable checkpoint is checkpoint:28d5d47e-cf10-286b-23ca-94dda6b39e7f.

claims.value: Dump 01 lines 1-226 reproduce the prior factory-planning export with formatting differences and omitted attachment stanzas, adding no unique conversation content. Dump 02 lines 1-96 share that opening through the Fabricator v2 Tube question; its unique span is lines 99-249, covering app origin, later-game scaling preferences, installed-state corrections, freight conventions, and Cargo Dispatcher ideas. Dump 03 lines 2-91 share the factory opening and line 229 repeats the final prompt-export request; its unique span is lines 95-225, covering the exploration pivot, Copperfield death, food observations, the low-twitch combat constraint, and unresolved weapon/Yellowstone questions.

Direct first-person reports may establish player state, history, preferences, and observations. Questions establish goals or uncertainty, not the truth of their premises. Quoted assistant text remains recommendation rather than an independent player observation. Accepted plans remain distinct from installed or completed save state, and historical checkpoints cannot silently overwrite current unknowns.

The overlapping branches preserve no original timestamps, so chronology uses explicit narrative ordering rather than reconstructed dates. A historical checkpoint does not prove the save has not advanced. All three raw dumps remain intact as provenance, but repeated statements strengthen provenance while remaining one canonical fact; no duplicate facts or competing game-data snapshot are created.

The canonical promoted outputs are `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json` for best-current installed state; `models/rourke-update1-play-history__20260711.json` for historical checkpoints, incidents, and durable preferences; `Player save - play history.md` for the human-readable gameplay timeline; and `Player-derived product requirements.md` for evidence-derived iOS requirements without treating every idea as an MVP feature. The earlier ZIP import remains canonical for its screenshots, generated reports, and more complete first factory-planning transcript.

answer.answer: Little Cloud is a modest fight, but your carried supplies make the consequences expensive. Bank excess ammunition and consumables if storage is reasonably close; otherwise move carefully and establish a separate recovery cache before continuing. Starry Night is lower-threat, so clear any wanderers, take the final chest first, then loot the debris.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty. Within 250 units it has 13 persistent hostile spawn entries: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder, with no mapped Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration. These markers represent possible persistent population, not necessarily simultaneous attackers.

Because the player is carrying valuable ammunition and consumables, bank the excess first if returning to storage is reasonably quick. Otherwise proceed methodically, preserve an abort route, and stage replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials in a separate safe recovery cache; the nearby chamber alone does not replace lost equipment or make corpse recovery safe.

A claimed Regeneration Chamber shortens the return trip but is not a complete recovery system: a nearby respawn without replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials can still force a return to a stable base. Direct field evidence also records corruption disabling a contested base and taking its chamber offline, causing respawn at the starting launcher. That is one observed incident; the exact corruption threshold and universal chamber-disable rules remain unverified. Update 1 also makes carried weapons losable on death.

Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty, with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, although roaming enemies can still wander in. Its guaranteed final chest contains the Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module. Clear wanderers, open that chest first, then loot the debris.

answer.answer: The first Geo Scanner became a durable recovery lesson: remote defenses must be fully powered and recovery supplies must survive the loss of the contested base itself. The encounter documents what happened once, but does not establish a universal corruption mechanic. The loot report remains intentionally unresolved.

claims.value: The first Geo Scanner defense required three attempts. After the first death, the player respawned at a nearby claimed base that had no replacement weapons or materials, forcing a walk back to Landerworks. On the second attempt, the temporary scanner fire base’s installed turrets were not powered; the player was overwhelmed, corruption disabled the base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber, and the next respawn occurred at the starting launcher. The third attempt succeeded.

The successful intervention was a fully built-out scanner fire base with every turret powered. Its automated defense defeated the assault and produced a strongly positive payoff—the player described the turrets as “singing” against the enemy.

The two deaths, empty nearby recovery point, unpowered turrets, corruption-disabled fire base and Regeneration Chamber, starting-launcher respawn, and powered-turret success are direct player observations from this encounter. They do not establish a universal corruption threshold or every condition under which corruption disables a Regeneration Chamber.

For future scanner defenses: stock replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials at the remote staging area; keep the only recovery cache outside the contested base’s corruption failure domain; power and function-check every turret before activation; and plan the worst-case respawn and return route. The completed scanner appeared to yield two unusually good food-related rewards or stacks, possibly involving a quantity of 20, but the dictated wording does not establish the exact items or counts; the completed scanner’s identity and coordinates also remain unresolved.

answer.answer: Landmark-grounded geography checkpoint completed and persisted as checkpoint:d3b40455-c7d9-2647-17a5-ed01b6da3d25.

claims.value: Grand Basin Reserve is the basin area north of the active corridor, immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry”; Mythic Cry is the mountain POI immediately west at approximately `2518.767,3099.107`. The older provisional match to the Red Lake/Redleaf basin was wrong and is superseded. The Grand Basin marker denotes the basin area, not a future Core; the first active campus is proposed east of Mythic Cry on the basin side of the terrain boundary.

Flowworks is a selected proposed footprint between Landerworks and Faraday: east/northeast of Landerworks and west/northwest of Faraday. Landerworks is beside the initial lander in the western/southwestern production corridor, while Faraday is immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn” and east/southeast of Flowworks. Flowworks is not a placed Core.

North is up, but the overview’s dashed site axis and site pins express relational, visually terrain-registered placement rather than surveyed rail geometry. Only Landerworks has a directly visible base pin; Flowworks is a proposed footprint, Faraday is terrain-registered rather than directly labeled in its crop, Grand Basin marks an area rather than a Core, and Sunstone Station and Brimstone Utility have relational grounding with exact pins still open. SRDB coordinates identify database markers and must not be combined with screenshot registration unless a transform is independently verified.

The preferred first Goethite satellite is the safer northwestern triple at approximately `1393–1464,1838–1891`, northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin. It is preferred over the closer western field around `1252–1472,2950–3282` because that field overlaps scanner/hostile envelopes. The plan is three Laser Drills merged locally into one Goethite-only Cargo link carrying 45 raw Ore/min. The preferred first Oil satellite is approximately `1234,3760`, west/southwest of Mythic Cry and Grand Basin: one Oil Extractor and one Crude-only Cargo link carrying 10 Crude/min to one GB-A Refinery. One Refinery consumes the full source plus large Titanium and Calcium feeds, so a second extraction source would require duplicating the expensive refining line; the marker around `1351,4473` is a separate site, not a same-pad extension. Raw resources are shipped because Goethite and Crude Oil are compact at extraction and expand heavily during processing; processing belongs beside Grand Basin consumers.

answer.answer: The Watch Session design is ready to resume as an evidence-bounded proposal: it prioritizes the next meaningful event, treats opportunities independently from cycle phases, and preserves conservative confidence, multimodal alerts, and explicit native-iOS permissions. Exact timing claims still require live Hotfix 0.2.8 validation.

claims.value: The design is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, Steam build 23761620, released 2026-06-17; structured-source capture SRDB 2.3.4, captured 2026-07-11; and a community/game-data model of 54 minutes from local fire-wave impact to the next impact. Creepy Jar has not published an official numerical phase formula. The 54-minute model is strongly corroborated by the current starrupture.tools client and an independent open-source mod reading game runtime, but it must remain versioned rather than presented as an eternal official invariant. Internal warning boundaries—approximately two minutes white, 15 seconds yellow, and a final roughly 15-second countdown—still require live Hotfix 0.2.8 validation. Use predicted, expected, favorable, and lower threat for community-derived transitions; never exact, safe, or guaranteed. Confidence states are Unsynced, Manual sync - predicted, Confirmed at one later transition, Drift suspected, and Cycle data changed - re-sync required. Do not invent numerical accuracy; downgrade confidence after a large correction, device-clock change, model-version change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Preserve the 54-minute engine model while presenting five player-meaningful states: Fire wave at 0:00-0:30 (0:30, remain sheltered); Cooling at 0:30-1:30 (1:00, remain sheltered); Recovery / quiet window at 1:30-11:30 (10:00, lower ambient threat and use the window); World active at 11:30-51:30 (about 40:00, ordinary enemies and ecology active); and Ruptura warning at 51:30-54:00 (about 2:30, return, bank loot, and shelter). Manual synchronization anchors 0:00 when the fire wall reaches the player. The portrait hierarchy, all visible without scrolling, is: sync/capability line; large semantic hero state and huge monospaced countdown; explicit countdown target; threat instruction and one action sentence; at most two opportunity cards; then exact local next-event times with Mute one cycle and Re-sync. During recovery, the hero target is when ordinary Vermin are expected to return; during normal ecology, it is the next Ruptura or warning-phase start. Retain a proportional whole-cycle rail for orientation, but also provide minimum/equal-width labeled steps or a next-events list so short Fire and Cooling phases remain legible. Color is supporting atmosphere only; text, symbols, and border treatments must carry meaning independently.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Opportunities are separately versioned evidence records, not automatic phase consequences. Each OpportunityWindow carries an id, start event or offset, end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot. Initial proposals are: reduced ordinary POI population during Recovery, with triggered encounters possibly persisting; Oxallop in early recovery while lakebeds are dry; cave access, Quartz, and Glowcaps during Recovery without guaranteed respawn; Ignitium immediately after Cooling through Recovery with variable spawn rate; Star Tears in late Recovery as experimental timing; Coralion/Vulpir eggs during post-wave Recovery with variable spawning; surface foliage and water as regrowth during the active world without exact species timers; and Sulheart hidden until exact current timing is validated. The Ignitium/Star Tears tradeoff should be explicit because community evidence indicates Star Tears mature on unharvested cooled Ignitium. Show no more than two prioritized cards, each stating what is favorable, the expected remaining window, and whether its evidence is confirmed, community-derived, player-observed, or experimental. The post-wave period is lower threat, not guaranteed safety: Geo Scanner, monolith, infection, Base Core, scripted POI, and other triggered encounters may ignore the environmental cycle.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Enemy-return and Ruptura alerts require distinct sounds and haptic signatures, while never relying on color or audio alone. The proposed enemy-return ladder is: 5 minutes, amber edge plus Finish or leave hard POIs, short double haptic/optional tone, and normal local notification; 2 minutes, persistent retreat banner, double tone/haptic, and optional notification; 1 minute, red instruction with emphasized seconds and a stronger distinct cue, background alert off by default; 15 seconds, static danger border, large seconds, one final cue, no ticking, and no background alert; event, ORDINARY VERMIN RETURNING with urgent triple cue and a local notification or explicitly armed alarm. Pre-Ruptura points are optional 10 minutes, 5 minutes, warning-phase start at 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. Support an exit buffer, Full/Haptic only/Visual only profiles, separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, Mute one cycle, and previews; after resume, never replay missed cues—collapse them to the strongest current-state message. Native behavior must disable the idle timer only while the monitor scene is active and then restore it, avoid background audio as keep-alive, schedule notifications at absolute dates and reschedule after anchor/model/policy changes, recompute state from (now - anchor) modulo cycle duration on resume, deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID, and limit Live Activity to the currently armed next event. AlarmKit on iOS 26 may break through Silent mode and Focus, but requires authorization, a usage description, and an explicit Arm action; never silently create a recurring 54-minute alarm. Earlier iOS versions use normal notifications; Time Sensitive is opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Preserve Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, stable sentence summaries, no flashing full-screen red, no default per-second ticking, visible capability state, and a visible exact next-alert time.

answer.answer: RuptureOps is not cleared for a corpus-backed public release. A public build may presently use only independently authored implementation with empty or synthetic data and newly created or separately licensed media; the current evidence also says the SwiftUI app has not yet been scaffolded. The SRDB-derived corpus and assets, imported packages, personalized player material, and benchmark binaries must remain private until explicit reuse permission or a separately licensed replacement strategy is established.

claims.value: The canonical corpus is derived from SRDB 2.3.4 and includes raw RSC/static captures, normalized data, the derived SQLite database, and 1,081 indexed asset references whose available binaries are privately mirrored in raw/assets.zip. Although robots.txt permits crawling, SRDB asserts copyright and publishes no explicit content/data reuse license. Therefore the mirrored dataset, normalized corpus, derived database, and mirrored assets are private research material and are not cleared for republication.

The private personalized boundary includes the Star Rupture Game Analysis import and its raw ZIP/extracted tree, duplicate third-party corpus, legacy SQLite database, player save baseline, personalized save context, player-specific planning and conversation-derived decisions, and nine player-specific site/geography assets. It also includes three user-authored prompt-history files totaling 58,207 bytes, 704 POSIX lines, 10,396 words, and 116 prompt delimiters; their promoted play-history model and associated player notes remain personal context. Player terrain, registration, and annotated-map screenshots—including world-map-named-sites.png and the dependent world-map-named-sites.svg/world-map-overview.png set—remain private.

No corpus-backed public app build is cleared now: the repository says the SwiftUI application has not been scaffolded and the iOS app is at planning/bootstrap stage. A safe public build can presently contain only independently authored implementation/code with empty or synthetic fixtures. It must exclude data/snapshots, data/star-rupture.sqlite3, data/snapshots/*/raw, mirrored source images/assets, imports, personalized models and notes, player screenshots, and the private evaluation fixture. The fixture’s binary site images, generated app icon, and warning audio are retained for a future multimodal/object-store lane and must not ship from this corpus; public images, icons, and audio must instead be newly created or independently licensed.

Before broader distribution, obtain separate reuse permission from the SRDB source owner that expressly covers redistribution of the normalized data, derived SQLite database, and mirrored assets, or replace them with a documented separately licensed-data strategy. The same clean-room boundary applies to media: use newly created or separately licensed images, icons, and audio, with license records, rather than imported player screenshots or fixture binaries. Until one of those paths is complete, keep the repository and corpus private and do not push the current corpus to a public remote.
